newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES PRESS HOME ADVANTAGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES PRESS HOME ADVANTAGE.

text.p: Fast bowler Ian Bishop snared the vital wicket of Australia all-rounder Steve Waugh to press home West Indies' advantage in the third test on Thursday.
Bishop removed Waugh for 58 to end a typically defiant innings by Australia's most resolute batsman and curtail the home side's recovery from a top order collapse on the opening day.
At tea, Australia were 155 for five after Waugh and his fellow all-rounder Greg Blewett added 102 runs for the fifth wicket at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Blewett remained unbeaten on 37 alongside wicketkeeper Ian Healy, who was not out on 19.
Australia, who lead the five-test series 2-0, were reduced to 27 for four before lunch after a hostile opening spell from veteran West Indies fast bowler Curtly Ambrose.
Ambrose claimed the wickets of captain Mark Taylor and his fellow opener Matthew Hayden and number four Mark Waugh during an accurate 10-over spell that yielded a miserly eight runs.
Taylor, whose side laboured to 55 for four at lunch, won the toss and elected to bat in fine conditions in front of more than 60,000 specatators.
Waugh, who missed the second test because of a groin injury, faced 131 deliveries during his 163-minute stay at the crease before edging a catch to wicketkeeper Junior Murray.
Ambrose doubled his meagre tally of three wickets from the first two tests during his burst with the new ball.
After removing opener Matthew Hayden for five, Ambrose accounted for Taylor and Mark Waugh with successive deliveries.
The unyielding pressure on the batsmen produced a further breakthrough when number three Justin Langer was run out for 12 after a breakdown in communications with Steve Waugh.
